title: Good Is the Lord, the Heavenly King
description: Good Is the Lord, the Heavenly King in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 65, part 5, headed “The blessing: of the spring; or, God gives rain. A psalm for the husbandman”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Good is the Lord, the heav-enly King, Who makes the earth his care, Vis-its the pas-tures ev-ery spring, And bids the grass ap-pear.

lines: Good is the Lord, the heavenly King,
Who makes the earth his care,
The clouds, like rivers rais'd on high,
Their watery blessings from the sky,
The soften'd ridges of the field
The little hills on every side
The meadows, drest in all their pride,
The barren clods, refresh'd with rain,
The parching grounds look green again,
The various months thy goodness crowns;
The bleating flocks spread o'er the downs,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
